references.text: The preceding context where Jesus posed the counter-question about John's baptism. The chief priests and scribes could not answer, so Jesus refused to answer them—as shown in [ref:Luk 20:3-7|Luke 20:3-7].
The parallel passage in [ref:Matt 21:27|Matthew 21:27] where Jesus gives the same answer to the Jewish leaders: "So I will not tell you by what authority I do these things."
The parallel passage in [ref:Mark 11:33|Mark 11:33] where Jesus similarly refuses to reveal the source of his authority, because his opponents refused to answer his question about John's baptism.

The original question from the chief priests and scribes in [ref:Luk 20:2|Luke 20:2], where they challenge Jesus regarding the authority by which he acts. Verse 8 is Jesus' final response to this question.

In [ref:Jer 38:15|Jeremiah 38:15] we see a similar pattern where a prophet hesitates to give an answer because the other party is unwilling to listen. Jesus knew that his opponents were not seeking the truth, so he chose not to reveal the source of his authority.

In [ref:Matt 16:1-4|Matthew 16:1-4] Jesus refuses to give the Pharisees and Sadducees the sign they ask for, because they ask with wrong motives. Similarly, here he refuses to answer because the question was not asked in sincerity.

In [ref:Joh 5:27|John 5:27] Jesus declares that the Father has given him authority. Although Jesus does not directly reveal the source of his authority in Luke 20:8, his entire ministry points back to the authority he received from the Father.
